== Problem ==

On the most recent exam on Prof. Xochi's class, 

* <imath>5</imath> students earned a score of at least <imath>95\%</imath>, 

* <imath>13</imath> students earned a score of at least <imath>90\%</imath>, 

* <imath>27</imath> students earned a score of at least <imath>85\%</imath>, 

* <imath>50</imath> students earned a score of at least <imath>80\%</imath>, 

How many students earned a score of at least <imath>80\%</imath> and less than <imath>90\%</imath>?

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 8\qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 14\qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 22\qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 37\qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 45 </imath>

== Solution 1 ==

<imath>50</imath> people scored at least <imath>80\%</imath>, and out of these <imath>50</imath> people, <imath>13</imath> of them earned a score that was not less than <imath>90\%</imath>, so the number of people that scored in between at least <imath>80\%</imath> and less than <imath>90\%</imath> is <imath>50-13 = \boxed{\text{(D)\ 37}}</imath>.

~DummyAMC

== Solution 2 ==

Let <imath>a</imath> denote the number of people who had a score of at least <imath>85</imath>, but less than <imath>90</imath>, and let <imath>b</imath> denote the number of people who had a score of at least <imath>80</imath> but less than <imath>85</imath>. Our answer is equal to <imath>a+b</imath>. We find <imath>a = 27 - 13 = 14</imath>, while <imath>b = 50 - 27 = 23</imath>. Thus, the answer is <imath>23 + 14 = \boxed{\text{(D)\ 37}}</imath>. 

-vockey
